Terrain lookup at a point. In: X = object (saved in $69), $64/$65 = X, $66/$67 = Y in pixels. Row = Y/8 indexes $0A80/$0AC0 (patched into $9956), column = X/8 indexes the row ($FF00 page, self-modified) to get a block number ($78), which picks a tile address from $1400/$1500 (patched into $9969); the char within the block, from the low bits of X and Y, gives a tile byte whose class $1600 selects $EB-$EE from the tables at $98E1. Returns X restored.
Self-modified operand bytes: $9956/$9957 take the row base from $0A80/$0AC0 ($9938/$993E); $9969/$996A take the tile address from $1400/$1500 ($995D/$9963). The rest of terrain_probe continues here.
High byte of the row base patched at $993E; the code after it reads the column index and fetches the tile address from $1400/$1500 into $9969/$996A (self-modified) before the class lookup.
Tile-address operand of LDX at $9968, patched from $1400/$1500; the tile byte read here indexes the class table $1600, which selects the four terrain properties $EB-$EE from $98E1-$990C.
High byte of the tile-address operand, patched from $1500 at $9963.
Object X = $1B70/$1BC0,X moved by $CB (bit 7 = left, low two bits = step; positive adds $CB) into $60/$61. $CB = 0 copies it unchanged.
Object Y = $1C10/$1C60,X moved by $CC (bit 7 = subtract low two bits; positive adds $CC) into $62/$63.
Called from $CA31/$CA47/$CD19. If $D5 is positive (stick up), probes the object centre ($9A09); if $EC is negative, sets state $1B20,X = 8, stops $CB/$CC and clears $A0D2.
Probes the terrain at the object centre: X + width/2 ($18F0,X) and Y + height/2 ($1940,X), then $990D.
Flag for $9A39/$9B4C: $FF when the probe one pixel above the leading edge found non-zero $EB.
Shared exit of the movement code: object state $1B20,X = 0 and $CB/$CC cleared (object stands still).

Horizontal movement against terrain for object X (callers $B2A5, $B5CE, $B82B, $C524, $C5A9, $CA15, $CF76). $CB = 0 stops (state 0). Probes the leading edge (right: X+width; left: X) and dispatches on $EB through a self-modified BPL chain ($9A6E, $9B61): free, step up/down, blocked, or special classes $0A/$0C which with $CC set start a climb (state 4 up / 6 down, $1E90,X = 1). Sets $DF to 5 or $82 for two classes (meaning open). Writes state $1B20,X and $CB/$CC, new position in $60-$63.

Operand of the BPL at $9A71, rewritten with $EB at $9A6E: a computed branch into the BPL chain $9A73-$9A7D, one landing per even $EB value (0 free, 2/4/6 step, 8 blocked, $0A/$0C special). Rest of move_walk (rightward) continues here.
Operand of the BPL at $9B64, rewritten with $EB at $9B61: computed branch into the chain $9B66-$9B72 for leftward walking (mirror of $9A72).

Callers as $9A39. If $CB differs from the facing $1DB0,X the object turns: $CB flipped, state 6, $CC=$81. Otherwise probes ahead at foot level and one row lower: blocked ahead gives state 2; no floor ($EC 0) stops (state 0); else steps down one pixel ($CC=1).
Copy of $CB kept by $9C5F.

Callers as $9A39. If $CB is set and differs from $1DB0,X, state 4 and $CC=1. Otherwise uses facing $1DB0,X and probes one pixel above the object at its leading corner using $ED/$EE (right/left) and $EB: open above moves up ($CC=$81, state $0C when nothing is under the trailing corner); blocked gives state 2 and clears $CB unless it was set.

Callers $C546, $C577, $C5C5, $CA27. Clears $75. With $CC set: moves Y ($99B8) and probes the head (up) or feet (down) at mid-width; $EC negative gives state 8, else $75=$FF and $CC=0. With $CC 0: when Y is not on an 8-pixel row forces $CC=$81; otherwise probes the corners ahead one pixel up (state 2 if blocked) and the centre ($EC positive gives state $0C).
Y MOD 8 of the object, stored by $9E0C: 0 selects the $EB test, otherwise $ED/$EE.

Callers $C5BF, $CA34. Probes the object's left and right edges at its current row (using $EB on a row boundary, $ED/$EE between rows) and nudges X one pixel towards the open side ($CB = 1 or $81), or $CB=0 when neither side decides.

Callers $A103, $A738, $A779, $A79B, $CCF9; body continues past $A000. Clears $75, moves X ($9985) and Y ($99B8) and probes the leading corners in the direction of $CB/$CC with $EB-$EE, setting $75 to $80 or $FF when blocked and stopping the move. Full semantics not traced here.

Tail of the object move/collision test s_9EC8 (entered from $9FFD with the up/left case): probes the map with j_990D at the object's next position ($64-$67 = x,y) using the per-object size tables $18F0 (width) and $1940 (height) and the tile flags $EC/$ED/$EE it returns; leaves $75 = 0 when the move is clear.
Shared exit of the move test: $75 = $80 (move refused by the solid-tile test, flags $EC/$ED). Callers read $75 as negative = cannot move.
Shared exit of the move test: $75 = $FF (move refused by the other flag test, $ED/$EE). What distinguishes $FF from $80 in play is not established; A0D4 treats $80 as landing and $FF as a stop.
Move test, left with no vertical component (from $9FAD): checks the tile at the object's top-left and bottom-left edges ($18F0 width) via j_990D; $75 = $80 if blocked.

Move test for a purely vertical move ($CB = 0, from $9EDB): $CC positive = up, negative = down; probes both bottom corners (down) or top corners with $1940 height (up) through j_990D and sets $75 = $FF if blocked.
Frame counter of the jump arc run by jump_arc_step: 0 = not jumping; counts up each frame; reset to 0 on landing. Also read at $9A05 and $CA07.
Horizontal direction ($CB) latched at take-off by jump_arc_step and reimposed every frame of the jump, so the direction cannot change in mid air.

One frame of a jump for object X (called from $CA44): on the first frame latches $CB and sets $1B20 (object 0 state) = $0A; vertical $CC = $01 (up) for frames 0-23, 0 for frames 24-39, then $81 (down) until blocked; moves through s_9EC8. On landing ($75 = $80) or $FF, clears the counter, stops $CC (and $CB on $80) and sets state $1B20,X = $0C.
One zero byte between jump_arc_step and the lift stop tables; no reference found by address search.
Lift (object $0E) stop positions, Y low byte, indexed by the stop number $F9 (0-7). Pairs with lift_stop_y_hi: Y = $0140,$01E0,$0300,$0400,$0440,$0480,$04C0,$0640.
Lift (object $0E) stop positions, Y high byte, indexed by $F9 (0-7); see lift_stop_y_lo.

Main-loop subsystem: the vertical lift, object $0E. While moving ($1B20+$0E <> 0) it steps Y by 2 in direction $F8 (via lift_step_y), carrying the Doctor (object 0) when $F7 is set; on reaching the stop in lift_stop_y_lo/hi[$F9] it plays sound $16, sets pause timer $FA = $7F, stops, and chooses the next stop (bounces between stop 0 and stop 7, $F8 = $02 up / $82 down). While stopped it counts $FA down; at $FA = 5 lift_check_board tests whether the Doctor is standing on it; at 0 it restarts. Every frame it ends in j_81DA (sprite update for X).

Sets $E0 = $FF when the Doctor (object 0) is within $3C horizontally and $10 vertically of the lift (object $0E, offset 7,8 pixels), else $E0 = 0. $E0 <> 0 suppresses the pocket keys in status_and_pockets.
Moves object X two pixels vertically: $CC positive adds 2 to Y ($1C10/$1C60), negative subtracts 2, zero does nothing. Used by the lift for itself and for the Doctor riding it.

Tests whether the Doctor (object X=0) stands on the lift (object $0E): within $96/$64 plays sound $16 (s_C7C7, only if $1B2E set), and if |dx| < $12 and |dy| = 8 exactly sets $1B20,X = 2, stops $CC and returns A = $FF (boarded); otherwise stops sound $16 when far and returns 0. Preserves $DA. Also called from $CAC8.
Horizontal mover (object $0F) end positions, X low byte, indexed by $FD (0-3): X = $0228,$0708,$0888,$0E48 with truck_stop_x_hi. $FD 0/1 is one track, 2/3 (via Y=3) the other.
Horizontal mover (object $0F) end positions, X high byte, indexed by $FD; see truck_stop_x_lo.
RTS used as the early exit of truck_update when zone $56 is 0.

Main-loop subsystem: the horizontal carrier, object $0F. First picks which of two tracks it serves from the mover's own X high byte ($1BC0+$0F < 8: stops 0/1, else stops 2/3, only on a change of track). Does nothing while zone $56 = 0. Moving: steps X by 2 in direction $FC, carrying the Doctor while $FB is set; plays sound $17 while the Doctor is within $96/$64. At an end stop: sound $17 off, pause $FE = $BE, flips $FD bit 0 and reverses $FC. At pause 5, truck_check_board decides whether the Doctor is aboard. Ends in j_81DA.

Sets $FB = $FF (and $1CB0 = $FF) when the Doctor is standing on the carrier: |dx| from carrier X+$0C < 8 and the Doctor's Y equals exactly $0450. The exact Y match means the Doctor must be at that one height.
Moves object X two pixels horizontally: $CB positive adds 2 to X ($1B70/$1BC0), negative subtracts 2.

Distance from object X to the point ($64/$65 = x, $66/$67 = y): |dx| to $D9/$DA with direction $DD ($81 when the object is right of the point, $01 left, 0 equal), |dy| to $DB/$DC with $DE ($81 below, $01 above, 0 equal). Called from many subsystems ($8382, $860F, $9097 and more).

Decides whether object X moves this frame: when aligned to the 8-pixel grid in both X and Y, or not moving ($1DB0 and $1DE0 both 0), returns Y = 0 when the frame counter $53 AND 7 equals the object's phase $1A70,X, else Y = $FF; when off-grid and moving returns Y = 1 (keep going). Used by the creature routines at $B25B-$B694 and elsewhere.
Moves object X one pixel along its current direction: $1DB0,X (horizontal, bit 7 = left) changes X $1B70/$1BC0, $1DE0,X (vertical, bit 7 = up (decrement)) changes Y $1C10/$1C60.

High byte ($04) shared by pocket_screen_lo and pocket_frame_lo.
Low bytes of the screen addresses ($0487-$049B, three characters each) under the five pockets where the selection marker is drawn: char $95 under the selected pocket, $97 under the others.
Low bytes of where the four markers are shown on the status bar ($0437,$0439,$045F,$0461), indexed by marker 0-3; two characters each; high byte marker_screen_hi.
High byte ($04) for marker_screen_lo.

Main-loop subsystem: status bar and the function keys. On frames with $53 AND 3 = 0 prints the 10-character name of the item the Doctor holds ($1D80 via offset table $1720 into names $1770) at $0453; on the other three frames prints one BCD byte of the score $57/$58/$59 as two digits (glyphs $1730) at $042F-$0434. Then, unless $E0 is set: F1 ($D0, edge-triggered by $D6) moves the pocket selector $3C round 0-4; F3 ($CF, edge $6A) puts the held item into a pocket or a marker slot (objects $30-$33) or, with empty hands, takes the selected one out (pocket_take); F7 ($D1) throws (throw_start) or with no direction sets $89; F5 ($D2) while standing still picks up (pickup_nearby).
Scratch: which marker slot (0-3) pocket_take found when pocket 0 (the marker pocket) is selected.

F3 with empty hands: takes the item in the selected pocket $3C (pocket 0 = the most recently stored marker, $42-$45) and tries to place it beside the Doctor via place_held_item; on success clears the pocket ($3D+$3C or the marker slot) and blanks its box on the status bar with char $94.
Clears pocket X ($3D,X = 0) and blanks its item graphic on the status bar (width $1960,Y by height $1990,Y characters of $94, upward from pocket_screen_lo). Also entered from $C143.

F7 and F5 handling for status_and_pockets. F7 with a direction held ($D4/$D5) throws the held item with $CB/$CC = direction+1 (so $02 or $82) through throw_start; F7 alone sets $89 = $FF. F5 when the Doctor is not moving ($1DB0, $1DE0 = 0) goes to pickup_nearby.
Two bytes $02,$82 (the right and left direction values) between the key handler and the throw code; no reference found.
RTS: exit of thrown_update when both flight slots are done.

Main-loop subsystem: objects in flight. Two slots (Y = 1,0): $46,Y object number, $48,Y frame count ($FF = free), $4A,Y horizontal and $4C,Y vertical direction. An object whose state $1B20 is no longer $0E frees its slot. Thrown level: flies flat until frame $30, then drops ($81) and falls faster ($82) from frame $60; thrown up: rises until frame $28. Code lock seed 2 (0-4), from the inverted frame counter; also selects the second clue.

Read at $BF07 (shifted, & 7) as the decoy value for the two wrong buttons; not written anywhere in $B000-$BFFF.

Code lock: the next correct digit, $BD38[$BD3E] ($BEF2).

Code lock deck, 186 bytes $BD6F-$BE28. Each byte is 8*a+b (a 0-4, b 0-5). The dealer finds the ($BD41+1)-th byte equal to 8*$BD3F+$BD40 and takes the low three bits of the six bytes from there as the sequence.
Code lock deck continued, $BDAF-$BDEE (see $BD6F).
Code lock deck continued, $BDEF-$BE28 (see $BD6F).

Empty-handed F5 in the code-lock room (Doctor x hi $0A), unless solved ($4E negative). Deal a new code: position 0, seeds $BD3F, $BD40, $BD41 from frame counter $53 (reduced mod 5), then search $BD6F and copy six digits to $BD38, then show buttons ($BEEC).

Character for the left button ($BF37).
Character for the middle button ($BF40).

Main-loop subsystem, runs only when $56 = 3 and every 8th frame; loads X=3 and Y=$52 (screen buffer) and reads $8788,Y; the body continues at $C000 outside this range.

Keeps four fixed cells drawn on both buffers.

Four object slots handled by fuse_update: $3D, $3C, $48, $4C (read as X by $C0C6; also read at $936F). $3D is special-cased (blast radius $80, only it can trigger the level rise or the tile change in blast_damage).

Per fuse slot (index Y 0-3, objects fuse_object_ids): $FF idle; set to $0F when a fuse burns out, then counted down once per call by blast_countdown_step; at 8 the blast damages, at 0 the object is retired. Also read at $9379.

Main-loop subsystem. If the rising level $51 is non-zero: starts sound 3 and every 128 frames increments $51; if $51 then exceeds the Doctor's Y/8 ($1C60:$1C10 >> 3) sets $E8=8 (death cause 4). Then for fuse slots 3..1: a slot counting down (fuse_countdown bit 7 clear) runs blast_countdown_step; else an object whose $1CB0 is non-zero runs fuse_tick; only the first active slot is serviced. Finally slot 0 (object $3D) likewise.

Fuse slot Y, object X. Decrements fuse_countdown,Y; at 8 calls blast_damage. Copies the object's position to object $2B and draws it (JMP $81DA with X=$2B): the explosion sprite. At 0: an object in mode ($1B20) 2 clears $1D80 (the Doctor's held object); mode 0 with $83 free posts X to $82 with $83=1; other modes remove it from the pocket list $3D-$42 via $A656. Then sets mode 4 and the slot idle ($FF).
While the fuse object X (mode not 4) burns: picks fuse_frame_on or fuse_frame_off by $53 AND fuse_flash_mask,Y into $1D30,X and draws it via $81DA.

Fuse slot Y, object X with $1CB0,X > 0 (the fuse time). Every other frame decrements $1CB0,X; while non-zero shows the flashing frame. At zero: if the object is in mode 4 it takes the Doctor's position; starts the slot's countdown ($0F) and its sound (fuse_sound); sets blast_radius $20, or $80 for object $3D.

Object X explodes. Every object Y=$2F..0 within blast_radius on X and $20 on Y (via $AC67 distance) gets $1CB0,Y=$14 (destroyed). Main-loop subsystem for the Doctor (object 0; also called from $FCFF, $FD19). Sets object 0's X from $20/$21 + $91. Scratch: fall distance high byte.
